title: Firewall
what: Controls inbound and outbound connections using rules.
protects: Limits access to unnecessary network ports.
limits: Cannot stop every malicious file or action by an allowed app.
guardboard: Shows UFW and nftables status when evidence is readable; does not change rules automatically.
example: Deny unnecessary inbound connections on a home computer.

title: Antivirus
what: Checks files against known malware signatures and rules.
limits: Cannot detect every new or hidden threat.
guardboard: Runs a local ClamAV scan on a folder you select.
example: Scan a downloaded project archive before opening it.

title: VPN
what: Routes traffic through an encrypted tunnel to a VPN server.
protects: Can reduce observation on the local network.
limits: The VPN provider may see activity; it does not guarantee anonymity.
guardboard: Reads active NetworkManager VPN connections; other methods may be missed.
example: Use a trusted VPN on untrusted Wi-Fi.

title: Tor
what: Routes connections through several volunteer relays.
protects: Can help obscure your network address when used correctly.
limits: App mistakes, account sign-ins, or misconfiguration can reveal identity.
guardboard: Tor management is not yet implemented; availability checks are planned.
example: Use Tor Browser for a privacy-sensitive site.

title: Intrusion detection
what: Looks for possible attack signs in logs and network activity.
limits: An indicator is not proof of an attack and may be a false positive.
guardboard: System sensor alerts exist; login indicators are not yet complete.
example: Notice a burst of failed sign-in attempts.

title: Linux hardening
what: Reviews services, permissions, and security settings carefully.
protects: Reduces exposure from unnecessary services and weak settings.
limits: One-time configuration cannot provide permanent protection.
guardboard: Checks are being expanded; system settings are not changed automatically.
example: Review SSH access and open ports regularly.

title: File integrity
what: Compares selected files' SHA-256 hashes with a prior baseline.
protects: Shows new, changed, or deleted project files.
limits: Does not prove who changed a file or why; the baseline also needs protection.
guardboard: Provides a local project baseline and comparison.
example: Detect an unexpected source file change.

title: Authentication
what: Checks the identity of a user or application.
limits: Stolen sessions or weak passwords can bypass it.
guardboard: Uses a random local session key and CSRF checks.
example: Use a unique long password for each account.

title: Multi-factor authentication
what: Requires a second factor beyond a password.
protects: Helps protect accounts after password exposure.
limits: Does not fully prevent phishing or session theft.
guardboard: GuardBoard has no accounts; it recommends MFA for important external accounts.
example: Enable a passkey or authenticator on GitHub.

title: Encryption
what: Makes data unreadable without the key.
protects: Can protect data on a lost disk.
limits: Malware may read data while the system is unlocked.
guardboard: Disk encryption evidence is not yet fully assessed.
example: Use LUKS disk encryption on a laptop.

title: Backups
what: Keeps recoverable copies of files in a separate location.
protects: Reduces damage from deletion, disk failure, and ransomware.
limits: An untested backup may not restore successfully.
guardboard: Automatic backup is not yet implemented; restore testing is planned.
example: Keep encrypted project backups on an external drive.

title: Network security
what: Observes connections, listening ports, and network boundaries.
protects: Helps spot unnecessary services and unusual connections.
limits: A visible connection alone does not prove malicious behavior.
guardboard: Shows local interfaces, traffic, and listening ports.
example: Find a service unexpectedly listening on 0.0.0.0.

title: Wi-Fi protection
what: Reviews wireless security and adapter state.
protects: Helps identify open networks and weak signal conditions.
limits: Signal strength does not reveal exact physical distance.
guardboard: Shows the current adapter, nearby networks, and channel usage.
example: Choose WPA2/WPA3 Wi-Fi instead of an open network.

title: System updates
what: Installs fixes for known software and system defects.
limits: Cannot eliminate unknown flaws or bad configuration.
guardboard: Partly reads automatic update configuration; does not install packages.
